newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Clemency for Ivorian soldiers held for plotting.
newsitem.headline: Clemency for Ivorian soldiers held for plotting.

text.p: Ivory Coast's government has ordered the release of seven soldiers detained pending investigation of coup plot allegations, according to a statement from Defence Minister Bandama N'Gatta.

The statement, published in the government newspaper Fraternite Matin on Saturday, said that the release order came after President Henri Konan Bedie accorded them clemency as part of efforts to build "a society based on peace and tolerance".
The soldiers have all been dismissed from the army. That sanction remains.
The coup plot allegations date back to Bedie's October 1995 election, a poll boycotted by the main opposition and surrounded by ethnic and political unrest which killed 35 people.

General Robert Guei was sacked as army chief of staff on the eve of the poll after not ordering the army on to the streets. He was dismissed from the army last January 29 after a military enquiry accused him of serious faults of discipline.
Guei, who served as sports minister in Bedie's government after being sacked, has never been formally arrested.
